description: We are a passionate and collaborative team joining NASA Space Apps 2026 in Legazpi City. We aim to use NASA data, Earth observation, AI, and technology. We welcome members skilled or interested in data analysis, agriculture, Earth science, AI/ML, software and web development, design, and storytelling. Curiosity, creativity, and teamwork are always welcome!
summary:
Rainfed farmers in Bicol need to know what they can plant between harvests when water availability and planting windows vary. We built AMIHAN (Adaptive Multi-season Insights for Harvest and Agricultural Needs), a web app that helps farmers and agricultural extension workers compare planting dates and crop rotations. It combines NASA rainfall and soil moisture records with local crop calendars and field observations such as drainage, water access, and crop history.

Our pilot focuses on Pamplona, Camarines Sur. AMIHAN helps users check whether mungbean can be planted, picked, and cleared after a rice harvest while leaving enough time to prepare the field for the next rice crop. Farmers and extension workers can use the result to discuss whether an extra crop fits and what conditions they need to check before planting.
details:
We built AMIHAN for rainfed farmers and agricultural extension workers in the Bicol Region of the Philippines. It helps answer a practical question: given the last harvest, the water available, and the next planned crop, what can we grow in the time we have?

In Crop Planner, users select a town or pin a field, choose a planting date, and enter their previous crop, harvest date, water source, and drainage. The planner combines local planting calendars and crop growth timelines with those answers to show planting and harvest windows. It also tells users which field conditions they still need to check. The app includes a 48-crop library, a watering guide, and a downloadable planting guide that can be saved for offline reference.

Our Pamplona pilot builds on Department of Agriculture Region V trials of mungbean after rainfed rice. The creative step is turning a regional crop calendar into a field-level timing check. AMIHAN accounts for the paddy draining after rice harvest, the moisture needed to establish mungbean, and the time needed for final picking and field preparation before the next rice planting.

NASA GPM IMERG provides historical rainfall patterns. NASA POWER supplies the weather archive, and SMAP provides regional root-zone soil moisture comparisons. On the Field Map, NASA Harmonized Landsat and Sentinel-2 imagery lets users explore vegetation greenness near a selected pin. We accounted for the scale of the satellite and terrain data by asking users to confirm conditions such as drainage and soil moisture in the field.

We built the web app with React, TypeScript, Vite, and Tailwind CSS. We used Three.js for the interactive terrain map, Recharts for climate charts, and Node.js and Python scripts to prepare data. The intended impact is to give farmers and extension workers a practical way to discuss a second crop, spot timing and water constraints early, and take a planting plan back to the field.
